label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: a register for every number, a check every change passes, a site to work on, and a brief with a file beside it
findings.why: As someone with one finished app and no coding background, I meet register, check, site and brief as four unexplained terms before any of them is shown.

findings.quote: Most held, some only in part, some had not been checked yet, and three did not hold.
findings.why: The sentence reads out the figure that the stacked bar at line 28 then draws again.

findings.quote: A claim without a captured source is a gap, and the register says so rather than leaving it out. Gaps are allowed. Hiding them is not.
findings.why: Three short sentences in a row, ending on a tidy contrast, where one longer sentence would carry the thought.

findings.quote: no code loaded from elsewhere; every script parses; every beat has a slide
findings.why: I cannot tell what 'parses' or 'beat' means, and the list is the first place I need to see what a check actually is.

findings.quote: Put the two side by side and half of the page is the check said in words.
findings.why: It sends me to chapter 4's page of rules, which I have not read here, so I cannot do the comparison it asks for.

findings.quote: A member that is certain its work is fine still has to pass the same test as one that is not.
findings.why: 'Member' is the team's word for an agent and is not explained on this page.

findings.quote: Chapter 5 has the example I like best
findings.why: The refused release is mentioned here only to point away, which leaves the claim without its scene.

findings.quote: One check that every change has to pass is where all of this begins.
findings.why: This is the step I came for, and it gives me no concrete first check I could set up after my one app, nor what to type or ask for.

findings.quote: the player, from ruv.sgit.ai, working on an iPad
findings.why: The player and ruv.sgit.ai are used as known things, so I am not sure what is being built or where it lives.

findings.quote: ruv-sgit went from one run an hour to several at once
findings.why: ruv-sgit appears without an introduction, and I cannot tell whether it is a person, an agent or a site.

findings.quote: I looked, I asked, they changed it, and I looked again.
findings.why: The loop is told here and then named again at line 124 as think, explain, create, review.

findings.quote: It looks a lot like an OODA loop, and maybe it is a variation on it
findings.why: OODA is not explained, and as a non-coder I skim past it.

findings.quote: write your list with the most important thing first, and note each time you reorder it
findings.why: It is a gentle, doable step, but it is about to-do lists and not about my app, so it feels distant from the next step I wanted.

findings.quote: I like how it said so to deck:
findings.why: Deck is not yet introduced to a reader who skipped earlier chapters, and the 'I like' is a gloss on the quote, not a thought.

findings.quote: The line is the honest heart of a map like that
findings.why: It tells me how to rate the line and not what the map does, which is a small steer on the reader's judgement.

findings.quote: Then it goes to the editor, as the strongest objection to his own part one. Not buried.
findings.why: The same decision is stated again at line 79 and in the closing card at line 94, three tellings of one idea.

findings.quote: ask one of your agents to argue against your plan, in writing
findings.why: This is the most usable idea for me, but it does not say which tool or how to ask, and I have only built one app.

what_holds: 11-the-plumbing.md: the four-pipe opening promises something I can build, and keeping the failure of the empty corrections file in is honest and memorable.
12-the-creator-comes-back.md: the conductor turning down the plan at the moment of most pressure is a clear scene about checks that I can picture.

13-the-story-before-the-slides.md: the researcher saying a line does not hold, and the editor keeping it anyway with the objection on the record, is a strong example of deciding with the argument in front of you.
notes: As a first-build finisher I am looking for my next step, and these chapters describe a nine-hour team of named agents with a vocabulary (member, wake, register, brief) I only half follow. The Something to try cards are the part I could act on, but they are thin next to the chapters. I would read on to find the first concrete start, and I would be put off if the cards stay this general.
